apis.measures: the largest, over the frames of the last second, of the time from before MainLoop::process to after RenderingServer::draw
apis.used: recorded in each sample as a cross-check; not in the total

apis.measures: the largest time of a physics iteration
the CPU clock between the renderer's stamps at the start and the end of the viewport's render
apis.describes: a draw 6 draws earlier on the Compatibility renderer

apis.measures: the scene and canvas updates before the viewports render
apis.describes: the last completed draw (the frame's own at frame_post_draw)

apis.measures: the monotonic clock in microseconds (mach_absolute_time): elapsed time and not the thread's CPU time
apis.waitForDisplay: depends on where it is called
apis.used: stamps at process_frame, frame_pre_draw, physics_frame and the last _process and _physics_process

terms.process_ms: process_frame to frame_pre_draw (a frame that does not draw: to the last _process)
terms.setup_ms: get_frame_setup_time_cpu of the frame's draw, read at frame_post_draw
terms.render_ms: viewport_get_measured_render_time_cpu for the frame's draw, read RENDER_READING_LAG_DRAWS = 6 draws later

formula.headless: no draw: setup_ms and render_ms are 0 and the total is physics_ms + process_ms
formula.accuracyRule: |median(total over the measured frames of load-T) - base - T| <= 0.1 T, base = median of the total over the measured frames of every idle block

artifactNote: The raw reports are not committed (docs/evidence/**/*-report.json is ignored and the receipts are large); their SHA-256 are above, and the windowed receipt keeps every frame of the run under raw. Anyone can apply another rule to them with node tests/cpu-time-instrument-native.test.mjs --replay=<report> (headless) or node scripts/cpu-time-instrument-graphics.mjs --replay=<raw> (windowed).
findings: Performance.TIME_PROCESS is set once a second, to the largest process time of the second, and with the vsync on it holds the wait for the display: the median of an idle window's TIME_PROCESS is 14 to 16 ms where the instrument reads 0.08 ms.
A busy loop of 2 or 5 ms does not show in the interval between frames headless (the loop's sleep paces it at 6.9 ms), and in a window the interval is the display's clusters.
The render reading of a draw arrives 6 draws later on the Compatibility renderer of 4.7.2 on macOS; the render pulse lands there and nowhere else.
The instrument reads the four loads to within 0.2% headless and 1.5% in a presented window.
decisions: The per-frame process term is a clock stamp at the engine's hooks and not Performance.TIME_PROCESS, which the spec assumed per frame.
TIME_PROCESS is recorded in every sample and the oracle checks it against the instrument's series (never under it between two of its changes).
The windowed lane is one run, judged by the baseline's idle reference; a window that no display presented is reported as not presented and claims no accuracy.
The threshold is not frozen: this record pins the instrument, its verification and the recommendation, and the freeze is a later single act.
limitations: Local macOS arm64 evidence; hosted CI is pending and the windowed lane and the sabotages are local only.

The clock is monotonic elapsed time, not the CPU time of the thread: a thread that the system descheduled between two stamps counts that time. The Mac was loaded by other agents (load average 5.5 to 9.9).

The render term was exercised by a canvas item of 30,000 rectangles in a lab scene, six draws late, on the Compatibility renderer, one display and one vsync mode; not by the Frontier game or either HUD.
The arms of the comparison (A, B and C) do not carry the instrument yet and arm B does not exist; the iPhone depends on the V05-09 decision; the vsync disabled lane and a render thread were not run.
The threshold cpu-time-instrument is not frozen (frozenValue null).
